name: InterContinental Barcelona
positioning: A luxury city hotel at the foot of Montjuïc, with a rooftop terrace and glass pool overlooking Barcelona, a spa and a MICHELIN-starred restaurant
best_for: Travelers who want a quieter base near Montjuïc, its museums and the Fira Barcelona Convention Center
Guests who want rooftop pool time with panoramic city views
Food lovers drawn to a MICHELIN-starred hotel restaurant

facts.text: The hotel is at Avenida Rius i Taulet 1-3 in Barcelona.
The hotel is a base for outdoor activities in Montjuïc, the Joan Miró museum, the Mies van der Rohe Pavilion and the Fira Barcelona Convention Center.
Poble Espanyol is about 0.85 kilometers from the hotel.
The interior common areas are airy, with high ceilings and statement art pieces.
Rooms have a classic beige, white and blue color scheme.
Classic Room bathrooms have a separate bath, a walk-in rain shower and a bidet.
The Presidential Suite has a living-dining area with a kitchen and two bedrooms.
Spa therapists use techniques borrowed from India and the East.
The spa has water jets and hot-stone beds.
Restaurant QUIRAT was awarded a MICHELIN star in 2026.
QUIRAT uses seasonal and sustainable ingredients, many from its own garden.
An urban rooftop garden supplies home-grown herbs and aromatic plants to the hotel's restaurants.

highlights.text: The 173 Rooftop Terrace has a swimming pool, views, drinks and Mediterranean flavors.
From the rooftop guests can see Barcelona from the Torre de Collserola and Tibidabo to the Montjuïc cable car, the Sagrada Familia, the cathedral and the Palacio Nacional.
The rooftop has a glass swimming pool and panoramic views.
Some Classic Rooms come with access to the Club InterContinental lounge.
The spa offers Natura Bissé treatments.

considerations.text: The Poble Sec district does not attract as much tourist traffic as its neighbors; the hotel is a short metro or taxi ride from the city's main tourist attractions.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: InterContinental Barcelona, an IHG Hotel
